title: Solving the Equation floor(x) = ceiling(x)
originalTopic: The Greatest and Least Integer Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine all real numbers x that satisfy the equation floor(x) = ceiling(x).

steps.title: Test Integer Values of x
steps.explanation: If x = n is an integer, the greatest integer less than or equal to n is n itself, and the least integer greater than or equal to n is also n. Thus floor(x) = ceiling(x) for every integer.
steps.why: Every integer is both <= itself and >= itself.

steps.title: Test Non-Integer Values of x
steps.mathExpression: x \notin \mathbb{Z} \implies \exists n \in \mathbb{Z} \text{ such that } n < x < n + 1
steps.explanation: If x is not an integer, x lies strictly between two consecutive integers n and n + 1. Then floor(x) = n while ceiling(x) = n + 1, so ceiling(x) - floor(x) = 1 != 0.
steps.why: For any non-integer real number, the floor and ceiling always differ by 1.

steps.title: Conclude the Solution Set
steps.explanation: The equation floor(x) = ceiling(x) holds if and only if x is an integer.
steps.why: Combining the two exhaustive cases (x in Z and x not in Z) proves that Z is the complete solution set.
